* Principal deity: {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Tomihayayae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}
* Right auxiliary shrine: {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ca|Ōkuninushi|es|Ōkuninushi|fa|اوکونینوشی|fr|Ōkuninushi|hu|Ókuninusi|id|Ookuninushi|it|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|ko|오오쿠니누시|mni|ꯑꯣꯀꯨꯅꯤꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Ōkuninushi|pt|Ookuninushi|ru|Окунинуси|simple|Ōkuninushi|sr|Okuninuši|sv|Ōkuninushi|tr|Ōkuninushi|uk|Окунінуші|vi|Ōkuninushi|zh|大國主|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}
* Left auxiliary shrine: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}

The name “{{Ruby|Takachi|たかち}}” is an ancient toponym unrelated to the present-day place name of Kōchi City (which developed during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|new|इदो काल|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} through the changes Kawauchi → Taka-chi → Kōchi<ref>“Kōchi Castle,” ''Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 40: Place Names of Kōchi Prefecture'', Heibonsha, 1983.</ref>). In historical sources it also appears as “Takaji” or “Takamochi”{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Its origin is unclear, but ''Tosa no Kuni Shikishakō'' points out a phonetic correspondence between “Takachi” and “Takaichi” (in {{ill|Yamato Province|be|Ямата (правінцыя)|ca|Província de Yamato|ckb|پارێزگای یەماتۆ|cs|Provincie Jamato|de|Provinz Yamato|el|Επαρχία Γιαμάτο|es|Provincia de Yamato|fa|ولایت یاماتو|fi|Yamaton provinssi|fr|Province de Yamato|gl|Provincia de Yamato|hak|Yamato-koet|id|Provinsi Yamato|it|Yamato (provincia)|ja|大和国|ko|야마토국|lt|Jamato žemė|nl|Yamato (provincie)|no|Yamato (provins)|pt|Província de Yamato|ro|Provincia Yamato|ru|Ямато (провинция)|simple|Yamato Province|sk|Jamato (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамато|th|แคว้นยามาโตะ|tr|Yamato (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямато|ur|یاماتو صوبہ|zh|大和國|zh_min_nan|Yamato-kok|zh_yue|大和國|qid=Q907495}} {{ill|Takaichi District, Nara|ar|تاكايشي|ca|Districte de Takaichi|ceb|Takaichi-gun|es|Distrito de Takaichi|fa|منطقه تاکاایچی، نارا|fr|District de Takaichi|id|Distrik Takaichi, Nara|it|Distretto di Takaichi|ja|高市郡|ko|다카이치군|nl|Takaichi (district)|pl|Powiat Takaichi|ru|Такаити|zh|高市郡|qid=Q1117901}} there is {{ill|Kawamata Shrine (Q11553360)|ja|河俣神社|qid=Q11553360|lt=Kamo Kotoshironushi Shrine}}){{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

According to ''Tosa no Kuni Shikishakō'', the {{ill|Shintai|de|Shintai|el|Σίνταϊ|es|Shintai|fa|شین‌تای|fi|Shintai|fr|Shintai|hr|Shintai|id|Shintai|it|Shintai|ja|神体|jv|Shintai|ko|신체 (신토)|mk|Шинтаи|pl|Go-shintai|pt|Shintai|ru|Синтай (синтоизм)|simple|Shintai|sr|Шинтаи|tr|Shintai|uk|Сінтай (синто)|zh|神體|qid=Q327532}} of the principal deity is a blue-black jade stone; that of the left auxiliary deity is a blue stone; and that of the right auxiliary deity is a wooden statue{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}.

== History ==
The date of founding is unknown{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. Nearby stood one of Kōchi Prefecture’s representative tumuli, the {{ill|Hirata Sogayama Kofun|ja|平田曽我山古墳|zh|平田曾我山古墳|qid=Q22120134}} (now lost), and a theory has been proposed that this kofun and the shrine together formed the tomb and ritual site of the {{ill|Hata no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|波多国造|qid=Q21654186}}{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The ''{{ill|Kujiki|ar|كجيكي|fa|کوجیکی (سندای کوجی هونگی)|fr|Kujiki|id|Kujiki|it|Kujiki|ja|先代旧事本紀|ko|선대구사본기|pt|Kujiki|ru|Кудзики|uk|Кудзікі|vi|Cựu sự kỷ|zh|先代舊事本紀|qid=Q2716751}}'' “{{ill|Kokuzo Hongi|ja|国造本紀|qid=Q133833194}}” records that during the reign of the 10th emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ar|الإمبراطور سوجين|arz|الامبراطور سوجين|azb|سوجین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Sujin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوجین|cs|Sudžin|de|Sujin|el|Αυτοκράτορας Σουτζίν|es|Sujin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوجین|fr|Sujin|hr|Sujin|id|Kaisar Sujin|it|Sujin|ja|崇神天皇|ka|სუძინი|ko|스진 천황|ms|Maharaja Sujin|nl|Sujin|pl|Sujin|pt|Sujin|ru|Император Судзин|sh|Car Sujin|simple|Emperor Sujin|sl|Cesar Sudžin|sr|Суџин|sv|Sujin|th|จักรพรรดิซูจิง|tl|Emperador Sujin|tr|Sujin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Судзін|uz|Imperator Sujin|vi|Thiên hoàng Sujin|yo|Emperor Sujin|zh|崇神天皇|zh_classical|崇神天皇|zh_min_nan|Suzin Thian-hông|zh_yue|崇神天皇|qid=Q333530}}, Amenokara-sumi-no-Mikoto was appointed Hata no Kuni no Miyatsuko, leading to a theory that the shrine was founded around this time, though details are unclear{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1987}}. Ritual remains have been identified within the precincts, and artifacts such as {{ill|Haji pottery|fr|Poterie Haji|ja|土師器|pt|Cerâmica Haji|uk|Кераміка Хаджі|zh|土師器|qid=Q5639938}}, {{ill|Sue pottery|ar|فخار سوي|de|Sue-Keramik|es|Cerámica Sue|fr|Poterie Sue|ja|須恵器|pt|Cerâmica Sue|qid=Q7634351}}, and jars from the {{ill|Heian period|ar|فترة هييآن|ast|Periodu Heian|az|Heyan dövrü|bcl|Panahon ni Heian|bg|Хеян|bn|হেইআন যুগ|br|Marevezh Heian|ca|Període Heian|ceb|Panahon sa Heian|cs|Období Heian|de|Heian-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Χεϊάν|eo|Epoko Heian|es|Período Heian|eu|Heian aroa|fa|دوره يىلى|uk|1768|ur|1768ء|uz|1768|vec|1768|vi|1768|vls|1768|vo|1768|wa|1768|war|1768|wuu|1768年|xmf|1768|yi|1768|zh|1768年|zh_min_nan|1768 nî|zh_yue|1768年|qid=Q7675}}) during the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|el|Περίοδος Έντο|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|new|इदो काल|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}} by the seventh-generation Sukumo Doi chief retainer {{ill|Yamauchi Ujiatsu|ja|山内氏篤|qid=Q11466439}} and his heir Ujimasa. It is a three-bay {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|fr|Nagare-zukuri|it|Nagare-zukuri|ja|流造|pl|Nagare-zukuri|ru|Нагарэ-дзукури|sv|Nagare-zukuri|zh|流造|qid=Q210684}} structure with a cypress-bark roof. The interior is divided into an inner and outer sanctuary. Some carvings—such as elephant-nose brackets, frog-leg struts, and decorative supports—date from an early Edo reconstruction. The building is designated a Protected Tangible Cultural Property of Kōchi Prefecture and is currently enshrined within a protective enclosure{{Sfn|Takachiniimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}<ref name="Kōchi Prefecture Main Hall"/><ref name="Sukumo City Main Hall"/>{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.

The {{ill|Quercus gilva|ca|Quercus gilva|ceb|Quercus gilva|fr|Quercus gilva|ja|イチイガシ|ka|Quercus gilva|ko|개가시나무|sv|Quercus gilva|uk|Quercus gilva|vi|Quercus gilva|war|Quercus gilva|zh|赤皮青冈|qid=Q3414213}} (Castanopsis cuspidata) in front of the shrine is the largest tree in the shrine grove, measuring 29.0 meters in height and estimated to be 400 years old. It is designated a Natural Monument of Sukumo City{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}<ref>On-site explanatory sign.</ref>.

== Cultural properties ==
== Kōchi Prefecture–designated cultural properties ==
* Protected Tangible Cultural Property
** Main hall (structure) – Edo period; rebuilt in Meiwa 5 (1768). Designated on February 15, 1955 (Shōwa 30)<ref name="Kōchi Prefecture Main Hall">[http://www.kochinet.ed.jp/bunkazai/details/110-2/110-2-07.htm Takachiza Shrine Main Hall] (Kōchi Prefecture website).</ref><ref name="Sukumo City Main Hall">[http://www.city.sukumo.kochi.jp/sbc/history/cultural/p002.html Takachiniimasu Shrine Main Hall] (Sukumo City website).</ref>{{Sfn|Cultural Properties of Sukumo City (Sukumo City History)}}.

== Sukumo City–designated cultural properties ==
* Protected Tangible Cultural Property
** Half-bodied lion statues – Works from the {{ill|Kamakura period|ar|فترة كاماكورا|be|Перыяд Камакура|bg|Камакура|bn|কামাকুরা যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی کاماکورا|cs|Období Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Zeit|eo|Kamakura-epoko|es|Período Kamakura|et|Kamakura ajastu|eu|Kamakura aroa|fa|دوره کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-kausi|fr|Époque de Kamakura|gl|Período Kamakura|he|תקופת קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-kor|id|Zaman Kamakura|it|Periodo Kamakura|ja|鎌倉時代|ko|가마쿠라 시대|lt|Kamakura laikotarpis|mn|Камакура эрин|nl|Kamakuraperiode|no|Kamakura-perioden|pt|Período Kamakura|ru|Период Камакура|simple|Kamakura period|sk|Obdobie Kamakura|sl|Obdobje Kamakura|sr|Камакура период|sv|Kamakura|th|ยุคคามากูระ|tl|Panahong Kamakura|tr|Kamakura Dönemi|uk|Період Камакура|vi|Thời kỳ Kamakura|wuu|镰仓时代|zh|鎌倉時代|zh_min_nan|Kamakura sî-tāi|zh_yue|鎌倉時代|qid=Q236205}}. Two Karajishi statues made of {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|arz|تشاميسيباريس اوبتوزا|bg|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ca|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ceb|Chamaecyparis obtusa|cs|Cypřišek tupolistý|da|Solcypres|de|Hinoki-Scheinzypresse|es|Chamaecyparis obtusa|eu|Japoniar altzifre|fa|سرو پاکوتاه|fi|Japaninsypressi|fr|Chamaecyparis obtusa|gl|Chamaecyparis obtusa|hak|Hî-nò-khì|hu|Hinoki hamisciprus|id|Chamaecyparis obtusa|is|Sólsýprus|it|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ja|ヒノキ|ko|편백|ml|ചമേസിപാരിസ് ഒബ്‌ടുസ|no|Solsypress|pl|Cyprysik tępołuskowy|pt|Chamaecyparis obtusa|ru|Кипарисовик туполистный|sv|Japansk ädelcypress|tr|Chamaecyparis obtusa|uk|Кипарисовик туполистий|vi|Chamaecyparis obtusa|war|Chamaecyparis obtusa|zh|日本扁柏|zh_min_nan|Píⁿ-peh|qid=Q917187}} wood, each 32.5 cm tall; both lack half of the body.
